findings.title: duckdb_vector_get_validity return typed uint64, but it returns a pointer (uint64_t*) and must be intp per the all-pointers-are-intp convention
findings.description: signatures["duckdb_vector_get_validity"] = uint64(intp) (ducklib.py:236; wrapper ducklib.py:1206-1209). In duckdb.h the function is `uint64_t *duckdb_vector_get_validity(duckdb_vector vector)` — the return value is a POINTER to the validity bitmask, not a scalar uint64. numbox's documented contract (numbox-surface.md §4: 'All pointers are intp') and every other pointer-returning binding in this file follow that rule: the sibling `duckdb_vector_get_data` (void*) is correctly typed intp at ducklib.py:235. Typing this pointer as uint64 also creates an internal mismatch: the validity pointer is consumed by `duckdb_validity_row_is_valid`, whose first (validity) parameter is correctly typed intp (ducklib.py:233). So `duckdb_validity_row_is_valid(duckdb_vector_get_validity(v), row)` passes a uint64 where intp is expected, forcing an unsafe uint64->int64 conversion at the call site.
findings.impact: Violates the intp-for-all-pointers contract for a pointer return value and mismatches its own consumer (duckdb_validity_row_is_valid expects intp). On a 64-bit host the bit pattern is preserved so values are not corrupted, but callers receive a value-typed integer for an address and must reinterpret it, and the unsafe uint64->int64 coercion between get_validity and validity_row_is_valid can surface as a numba typing friction (worst case a typing error, otherwise a silent unsafe cast).
findings.recommendation: Change the signature to `signatures["duckdb_vector_get_validity"] = intp(intp)` so the validity pointer return matches the all-pointers-are-intp convention and lines up with duckdb_validity_row_is_valid's intp validity parameter and duckdb_vector_get_data's intp return.

findings.title: idx_t typed as intp (signed) instead of uint64 in several count/index slots, inconsistent with the idx_t->uint64 convention and the rest of the file
findings.description: Several signatures encode duckdb.h `idx_t` (which is uint64_t) as intp (int64) rather than uint64, deviating from the documented idx_t->uint64 convention and from the file's own majority usage. Returns: duckdb_column_count = intp(intp) (ducklib.py:105), duckdb_data_chunk_get_column_count = intp(intp) (ducklib.py:155), duckdb_data_chunk_get_size = intp(intp) (ducklib.py:156), duckdb_row_count = intp(intp) (ducklib.py:225) — all return idx_t. Arguments: duckdb_data_chunk_get_vector = intp(intp, intp) (ducklib.py:157) — 2nd arg is `idx_t col_idx`; duckdb_validity_row_is_valid = int8(intp, intp) (ducklib.py:233) — 2nd arg is `idx_t row`. Contrast the rest of the file, which correctly uses uint64 for idx_t: e.g. duckdb_get_list_size/get_map_size/struct_type_child_count/nparams/rows_changed (returns) and duckdb_column_logical_type/column_name/get_list_child (idx_t args).
findings.impact: Functionally harmless on a 64-bit host for in-range values (row/column/chunk counts and column/row indices are far below 2^63, so signed/unsigned reinterpretation is a no-op). The defect is a correctness-of-convention inconsistency: the same C type is encoded two different ways across the file, and a signed encoding of an unsigned count would misbehave only at the (practically unreachable) >2^63 boundary.
findings.recommendation: Type all `idx_t` returns and arguments as uint64 for consistency with the convention: change ducklib.py:105, 155, 156, 225 return types to uint64; change the 2nd arg of ducklib.py:157 and ducklib.py:233 to uint64.

notes: Scope: COR of numbduck's use of the numbox contract at /home/erik/projects/numbduck/numbduck/ducklib.py and pybridge.py, cross-checked against numbox call.py/highlevel.py/lowlevel.py and the duckdb.h C API. Items examined and found SOUND: (1) struct-by-value tuple layouts vs duckdb.h — hugeint Tuple((uint64,int64)), uhugeint UniTuple(uint64,2), decimal Tuple((uint8,uint8,uint64,int64)) (24B), interval Tuple((int32,int32,int64)) (16B), blob/bit Tuple((intp,uint64)), varint Tuple((intp,uint64,int8)) (24B), and duckdb_result UniTuple(intp,6) (48B) all match the C struct field order/size; (2) the 16B INT/INT eightbyte repack for interval and the >16B byval+optnone/sret paths are handled by numbox _call_lib_func, and CLAUDE.md's 'hand-rolled intrinsics at ducklib.py:1525-1640' follow-up is stale (those lines do not exist; duckdb_bind_hugeint/uhugeint/interval/decimal already route through _call_lib_func at ducklib.py:1410-1431); (3) enum values DUCKDB_TYPE_* match duckdb.h, and VARINT/BIGNUM=35 dual-naming is correct; (4) cres vs cres_if_available is used correctly — version-variable symbols duckdb_create_varint/get_varint/scalar_function_set_init are gated, others use plain @cres; (5) duckdb_create_time_tz / create_time_tz_value / get_time_tz typed as uint64 are correct — duckdb_time_tz is an 8-byte single-uint64 struct passed/returned in a register. CONSIDERED BUT NOT REPORTED: (a) pybridge.py:66 get_unicode_data_p("SELECT 1") returns an interior pointer aliasing the numba string payload; this is SAFE here because the argument is a persistent Python str literal (held in co_consts) whose buffer numba's unicode unboxing aliases, and it is consumed on the very next line. (b) _call_lib_func_byval is used for the three by-value duckdb_result functions (duckdb_fetch_chunk ducklib.py:945, duckdb_result_return_type :1131, duckdb_result_statement_type :1137). The numbox docstring frames _call_lib_func_byval as the `func(T*)` (true-pointer) path and it passes a plain pointer without the SysV `byval` attribute / optnone that _call_lib_func adds for >16B by-value structs; this raised an ABI question on SysV x86-64 MEMORY-class passing. I did not report it as a defect because this path is exercised by merged, passing UDAF/fetch tests (per CLAUDE.md), which would fail on a real ABI mismatch; resolving it definitively requires runtime verification (not permitted here), so reporting it would be speculation against working evidence.
